summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication on CentOS Stream 10 across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (read-only standbys). node1 was initialized fresh, configured with wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, listen_addresses='*', a dedicated pg_hba.conf replication rule for the replicator role scoped to node2/node3 IPs, and firewalld opened on 5432/tcp. A replicator role was created and node2/node3 were provisioned via pg_basebackup -R (streaming, writing standby.signal + primary_conninfo automatically). Verified standbys are read-only (INSERT rejected) and see primary writes. Then ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (standbys first, primary last), capturing boot_id before/after each reboot to prove real restarts, confirming postgresql service and replication/recovery state recovered after each, and finally validating a fresh write on the primary replicated to both standbys post-restart.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server/contrib 16.14 on node1, node2, node3
Initialized PGDATA on node1 with postgresql-setup --initdb
Configured node1 postgresql.conf for replication (listen_addresses, wal_level, max_wal_senders, max_replication_slots, hot_standby)
Added pg_hba.conf rules on node1 permitting scram-sha-256 replication/connections from node2/node3 subnet
Opened firewalld port 5432/tcp on node1 (was blocking replication connections)
Started/enabled postgresql on node1, created 'replicator' REPLICATION role with a generated password
Created repl_test table and inserted a baseline row on the primary
Ran pg_basebackup -R from node2 and node3 against node1 to clone data dir and auto-configure standby.signal + primary_conninfo
Started/enabled postgresql on node2 and node3, verified pg_is_in_recovery()=t and pg_stat_replication shows both streaming
Verified standbys reject writes (read-only) and see primary-committed rows
Captured boot_id baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node2, then node3, then node1 one at a time via `reboot`, backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled each node until exec was available again and confirmed boot_id changed post-restart
Verified postgresql service active, recovery/replication status, and data integrity after each node's restart
Performed a final write on the primary after all restarts and confirmed it replicated to both standbys

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication established, node1 primary writable, node2/node3 read-only standbys
evidence.summary: node1 initialized and configured as primary, replicator role created, node2/node3 cloned via pg_basebackup -R and started as standbys; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both standbys in 'streaming' state

evidence.requirement: Standbys are read-only and reject writes
evidence.summary: pg_is_in_recovery() returns true on both standbys; INSERT attempt on node2 fails with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction'

evidence.requirement: Changes committed on primary are visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Rows inserted on node1 ('committed-after-setup' before restarts, 'post-restart-check' after all restarts) both appear identically on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bccb87ac captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect (subsequent call timed out); post-restart boot_id 5e74a3c5 differs; postgresql active, still in recovery, data intact, and primary shows it reconnected streaming

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 45c22b1f captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id a17aba97 differs; postgresql active, still in recovery, data intact, and primary shows it reconnected streaming

evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state, cluster quorum/health preserved throughout (both standbys healthy before and during primary restart)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 06339ff3 captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 826dd26d differs; postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery()=false (writable primary), both standbys reconnected streaming, and a new write replicated successfully afterward
